findings:
🟡 [elapsed-null-coerces-zero] MUST-FIX In `buildRunRows` (src/status/runs-fields.js and the codex mirror) the expression `Math.max(0, (terminal ? (endedEpoch === null ? null : endedEpoch) : now) - startedEpoch)` yields `null - startedEpoch` → negative → `Math.max` → `0` for a terminal manifest (final_status set) whose `ended_epoch`/`ended_at` are null, so `elapsed_s` reports 0 instead of null, violating plan §2.5 "unknown is null, never 0" (the inner `? null :` branch is dead code because the subsequent `Number.isNaN` check never fires). Impact: a finished run with no recorded end time is shown as having taken 0 seconds. Smallest fix: compute `const endEpoch = terminal ? endedEpoch : Math.floor(nowMs/1000);` then `entry.elapsed_s = (startedEpoch === null || endEpoch === null) ? null : Math.max(0, endEpoch - startedEpoch);` and add one fixture (final_status set, ended_epoch/ended_at null) asserting `elapsed_s === null` in status-runs-fields.test.sh; re-run sync-codex-plugin-skills.sh so the mirror matches.
🔵 [lineage-suite-writes-real-live-dir] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The unmodified hooks/tests/dispatch-lineage suite does not set AUTOPILOT_LIVE_DIR, so `status runs` now writes `runs-enrich-cursor.json` into the real live dir during that suite (fixture `dir` key, so the real cursor merely resets on the next genuine call; write is atomic tmp+rename, mode 0600, fail-open). Persisting under the resolved live dir is what the spec mandates, so the product is correct; the fix belongs in the suite (export AUTOPILOT_LIVE_DIR to a /dev/shm mktemp dir), which is outside R3's Allowed files — hand off to depth-0 / the owning row rather than block R3.
🔵 [cursor-on-finished-run-restarts] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `rotationPick` restarts at index 0 when the persisted cursor id is no longer live (run finished between calls), so under steady churn the tail of the live list can be revisited later than ceil(live/cap) calls. Spec's acceptance (9 static live fixtures, cap 4, 3 calls) is satisfied; a positional/next-id fallback is hardening for a later row.
🔵 [selector-object-shape] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Plain `runs --json` (and `--root`, `--enrich-cap`) still emits an array with only added fields; the object `{filter?,project?,runs,unscoped?}` appears only when `--project` or `--since` is given, which the spec itself requires (top-level `filter:{since}`, `unscoped` bucket). This honours §2.6; no change needed. Note `--tree` with those selectors correctly nests the tree under `runs`.
